# 1 Samuel Chapter 6 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 153r–153v | **Source Image:** 1SA_006_page_001.jpg, 1SA_006_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The ark of the LORD was in the territory of the Philistines for seven months.

**2** And the Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the ark of the LORD? Tell us how we should send it back to its place."

**3** They said, "If you are sending the ark of the God of Israel back, do not send it empty. You must return to Him a guilt offering. Then you will be healed, and it will be made known to you why His hand does not turn away from you."

**4** They said, "What guilt offering shall we return to Him?" And they said, "According to the number of the lords of the Philistines: five gold tumors and five gold mice, for one plague was upon all of you and upon your lords.

**5** Make images of your tumors and images of the mice that are destroying the land, and give glory to the God of Israel. Perhaps He will lighten His hand from upon you and from upon your gods and from upon your land.

**6** Why should you harden your hearts as Egypt and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? Was it not after He dealt severely with them that they sent them away, and they went?

**7** Now then, take and prepare one new cart and two nursing cows upon which no yoke has come. Yoke the cows to the cart, but take their calves away and pen them up at home.

**8** Take the ark of the LORD and set it upon the cart. Place the gold objects you are returning to Him as a guilt offering in a chest beside it. Then send it on its way.

**9** And watch: if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth-shemesh, then He has brought this great disaster upon us. But if not, then we shall know that it was not His hand that struck us — it was a chance thing that happened to us."

**10** The men did so. They took two nursing cows and yoked them to the cart and shut up their calves at home.

**11** They set the ark of the LORD upon the cart, along with the chest containing the gold mice and the images of their tumors.

**12** And the cows went straight on the road toward Beth-shemesh. They went along one highway, lowing as they went, and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. And the lords of the Philistines followed them to the border of Beth-shemesh.

**13** Now the people of Beth-shemesh were reaping the wheat harvest in the valley. They lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and they rejoiced to see it.

**14** The cart came into the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite and stopped beside a great stone. They split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows as a burnt offering to the LORD.

**15** The Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest that was with it, in which were the gold objects, and set them upon the great stone. And the men of Beth-shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices to the LORD on that day.

**16** The five lords of the Philistines saw it and returned to Ekron that same day.

**17** These are the gold tumors that the Philistines returned as a guilt offering to the LORD: one for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gath, one for Ekron.

**18** The gold mice corresponded to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, from the fortified city to the village of the open country, including the great stone upon which they set the ark of the LORD, which remains to this day in the field of Joshua the Beth-shemeshite.

**19** But He struck some of the men of Beth-shemesh because they had looked into the ark of the LORD. He struck down seventy men, and the people mourned because the LORD had struck the people with a great blow.

**20** The men of Beth-shemesh said, "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God? And to whom shall He go up from us?"

**21** They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath-jearim, saying, "The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up to you."

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Strong three-way agreement on structure (21 verses) and key theological elements. All three recognized the kavod wordplay connecting to chapter 4, the Exodus parallel in v. 6, and the experimental logic of the cow test. The textual crux in v. 19 was handled identically by LOGOS and PNEUMA (seventy), while EMET preserved the full MT reading.

---
## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

### Verse 1 — "field/territory"
- **EMET:** "in the field of the Philistines"
- **LOGOS:** "in the territory of the Philistines"
- **PNEUMA:** "in Philistine territory"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS — "territory" better captures the Hebrew sadeh in this geopolitical context.

### Verse 3 — "empty" vs. "empty-handed"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "do not send it empty"
- **PNEUMA:** "don't send it empty-handed"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS — "empty" applies to the ark being sent back without offering.

### Verse 6 — "harden" vs. "be stubborn"
- **EMET:** "make heavy your hearts"
- **LOGOS:** "harden your hearts"
- **PNEUMA:** "be stubborn like Egypt"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS — "harden your hearts" preserves the Exodus vocabulary (cf. Exod 8:15) while remaining clear.

### Verse 7 — "nursing ones" vs. "milk cows" vs. "nursing cows"
- **EMET:** "cows, nursing ones"
- **LOGOS:** "milk cows"
- **PNEUMA:** "cows that are nursing"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "nursing cows" — clearer than EMET, more precise than LOGOS.

### Verse 8 — "box" vs. "chest"
- **EMET:** "box"
- **LOGOS:** "box"
- **PNEUMA:** "chest"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "chest" — the Hebrew argaz (hapax legomenon) likely denotes a container larger than a simple box.

### Verse 9 — "evil" vs. "disaster"
- **EMET:** "this great evil"
- **LOGOS:** "this great evil"
- **PNEUMA:** "this disaster"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA uses "disaster" — the Hebrew ra'ah here denotes calamity, not moral evil.

### Verse 18 — "meadow" (abel) vs. "stone" (even)
- **EMET:** "great meadow" (following Ketiv abel)
- **LOGOS:** "great stone" (following Qere even)
- **PNEUMA:** "large stone"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA with "stone," harmonizing with v. 14. The Ketiv abel is noted but the Qere reading is more contextually coherent.

### Verse 19 — number struck
- **EMET:** "seventy men, fifty thousand men" (preserving full MT)
- **LOGOS:** "seventy men" (omitting "fifty thousand" as likely corruption)
- **PNEUMA:** "seventy of them" (same approach as LOGOS)
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows LOGOS/PNEUMA with "seventy men." The "fifty thousand" is widely regarded as a textual corruption — implausible for a small town.

### Verse 20 — "to whom shall He go up" vs. "where can we send Him"
- **EMET:** "unto whom shall he go up from upon us?"
- **LOGOS:** "to whom shall He go up from us?"
- **PNEUMA:** "Where can we send Him so He is no longer with us?"
- **Resolution:** SOPHIA follows EMET/LOGOS — the Hebrew "to whom" (el mi) is about transferring the ark's burden to another community, not about spatial direction.

— SOPHIA
